Installing the old wheel put a package literally named 'src' into
site-packages, which collides with any project that has its own src/
package (the post-commit hook failed with ModuleNotFoundError there).

- move code to a src/gitgotchi layout
- make pyproject.toml the single source of packaging metadata
- drop setup.py, requirements.txt and the root gitgotchi.py shim
- add python -m gitgotchi
- remove empty stub modules

- uninstall now actually removes the hook command (it only removed the

+import os
+import stat
+import subprocess
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+
+from gitgotchi.db.state_manager import StateManager
+from gitgotchi.hooks.installer import (
+    HOOK_START,
+    hooks_dir,
+    install_hooks,
+    uninstall_hooks,
+)
+
+LEGACY_HOOK = (
+    "#!/bin/sh\n"
+    "# GitGotchi post-commit hook\n"
+    '"/old/venv/bin/python" -m src.hooks.post_commit\n'
+)
+
+
+def hook_path(repo) -> Path:
+    return hooks_dir(repo) / "post-commit"
+
+
+def test_install_creates_executable_hook(repo):
+    assert install_hooks()
+
+    content = hook_path(repo).read_text()
+    assert content.startswith("#!/bin/sh\n")
+    assert HOOK_START in content
+    assert "-m gitgotchi.hooks.post_commit" in content
+    if os.name != "nt":
+        assert hook_path(repo).stat().st_mode & stat.S_IXUSR
+
+
+def test_install_is_idempotent(repo):
+    install_hooks()
+    first = hook_path(repo).read_text()
+    install_hooks()
+    assert hook_path(repo).read_text() == first
+
+
+def test_install_migrates_legacy_hook(repo):
+    hook_path(repo).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    hook_path(repo).write_text(LEGACY_HOOK)
+
+    install_hooks()
+
+    content = hook_path(repo).read_text()
+    assert "src.hooks.post_commit" not in content
+    assert content.count(HOOK_START) == 1
+
+
+def test_uninstall_removes_legacy_hook_completely(repo):
+    hook_path(repo).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    hook_path(repo).write_text(LEGACY_HOOK)
+
+    uninstall_hooks()
+
+    assert not hook_path(repo).exists()
+
+
+def test_uninstall_keeps_other_hooks(repo):
+    hook_path(repo).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    hook_path(repo).write_text("#!/bin/sh\necho other\n")
+
+    install_hooks()
+    uninstall_hooks()
+
+    assert hook_path(repo).read_text() == "#!/bin/sh\necho other\n"
+
+
+def test_respects_core_hooks_path(repo):
+    with repo.config_writer() as cw:
+        cw.set_value("core", "hooksPath", ".githooks")
+
+    install_hooks()
+
+    assert (Path(repo.working_tree_dir) / ".githooks" / "post-commit").exists()
+
+
+def test_commit_feeds_pet_end_to_end(repo):
+    install_hooks()
+    root = Path(repo.working_tree_dir)
+    (root / "src").mkdir()
+    (root / "src" / "__init__.py").write_text("")
+    (root / "app.py").write_text("print('boo')\n")
+
+    subprocess.run(["git", "add", "."], cwd=root, check=True)
+    subprocess.run(
+        ["git", "commit", "-q", "-m", "feat: summon the first spirit"],
+        cwd=root,
+        check=True,
+        capture_output=True,
+    )
+
+    stats = StateManager().get_pet_state()
+    assert stats.total_commits == 1
+    assert stats.lines_added == 1
+    assert repo.is_dirty(untracked_files=True) is False

+# Changelog
+
+## 0.2.0
+
+### Fixed
+
+- The package is now installed as `gitgotchi` instead of `src`. The old name collided with any
+  project that has its own `src/` package and made the post-commit hook fail there.
+- `gitgotchi uninstall` now really removes the hook (it used to leave the command behind).
+- Running a command from a subdirectory no longer creates a second, empty companion.
+- `.gitgotchi/` is excluded from git automatically so the database can't be committed by accident.
+- Mood now reflects how long it's been since the last commit when you check on your companion.
+- Angel was unreachable; quality is now scored from each commit (see README).
+- `gitgotchi story` uses a current Claude model and shows why when it falls back to a built-in story.
+- `.env` files are actually loaded.
+- `gitgotchi version` reports the real version.
+
+### Changed
+
+- Hooks respect `core.hooksPath` and git worktrees, and are kept alongside any existing hook.
+  Running `gitgotchi install` again updates an old hook in place.
+- Requires `anthropic>=1.0` and `typer>=0.12`.
+- Added `python -m gitgotchi`.
+
+## 0.1.3
+
+- PyPI README update.
+
+## 0.1.0 - 0.1.2
+
+- Initial release for the Kiroween Hackathon.

+import numpy as np
+
+from gitgotchi.render.raster import Form, render
+from gitgotchi.render.scene import backdrop, compose, ground_shadow
+
+WIDTH = 64
+HEIGHT = 48
+
+
+def render_scene(
+    form: Form,
+    t: float,
+    width: int = WIDTH,
+    height: int = HEIGHT,
+    stage: bool = True,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Render a form on its night-sky stage. Returns uint8 RGBA (h, w, 4)."""
+    frame = render(form, t, width, height, offset=(0.0, 0.12))
+    if not stage:
+        return compose(frame)
+    lift = form.pose(t).bob / 0.15
+    return compose(frame, backdrop(width, height, t), ground_shadow(width, height, lift))

+import subprocess
+from pathlib import Path
+

+
+
+def commit(repo, message, name="f.py"):
+    root = Path(repo.working_tree_dir)
+    (root / name).write_text(message)
+    subprocess.run(["git", "add", "."], cwd=root, check=True)
+    subprocess.run(["git", "commit", "-q", "-m", message], cwd=root, check=True)
+
+
+def test_haunt_feeds_commits_without_a_hook(repo):
+    commit(repo, "feat: before haunting")
+    haunting = Haunting(repo, StateManager())

+    commit(repo, "feat: while haunting", "g.py")
+    haunting.poll(100.0)
+    assert haunting.stats.total_commits == 0  # waiting for the hook

+"""Shareable pet card: the 3D scene plus stats, as a PNG."""
+from typing import Dict, Tuple
+

+

+from gitgotchi.pet.states import PetStats
+from gitgotchi.render import render_scene
+from gitgotchi.render.font import draw_text, text_width
+from gitgotchi.render.forms import form_for
+
+CARD_W, CARD_H = 240, 126
+SCENE_W, SCENE_H = 112, 84
+SCALE = 5
+
+BG_TOP = np.array([18, 10, 32], float)
+BG_BOTTOM = np.array([40, 20, 60], float)
+SHADOW = (8, 4, 14)
+
+
+def hex_rgb(color: str) -> Tuple[int, int, int]:
+    color = color.lstrip("#")
+    return tuple(int(color[i : i + 2], 16) for i in (0, 2, 4))
+
+
+def _bar(image, x, y, width, fraction, color):
+    image[y : y + 4, x : x + width, :3] = (60, 42, 82)
+    filled = int(round(max(0.0, min(1.0, fraction)) * width))
+    image[y : y + 4, x : x + filled, :3] = color
+    image[y, x : x + filled, :3] = np.minimum(255, np.array(color) + 50)
+
+
+def agent_line(agents: Dict[str, int], width: int) -> str:
+    """As many "NAME COUNT" pairs as fit, then "+N" for the rest."""
+    ranked = sorted(agents.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])
+    for shown in range(len(ranked), 0, -1):
+        line = " ".join(f"{n} {c:,}" for n, c in ranked[:shown])
+        if shown < len(ranked):
+            line += f" +{len(ranked) - shown}"
+        if text_width(line) <= width:
+            return line
+    return ranked[0][0][: width // 6]
+
+
+def make_card(stats: PetStats, repo_name: str, agents: Dict[str, int], t: float = 0.15) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Render the card at 1x pixel scale. Returns uint8 RGBA (126, 240, 4)."""
+    rows = np.linspace(0, 1, CARD_H)[:, None, None]
+    card = np.broadcast_to(BG_TOP * (1 - rows) + BG_BOTTOM * rows, (CARD_H, CARD_W, 3)).copy()
+    card = np.dstack([card, np.full((CARD_H, CARD_W), 255.0)])

+"""`gitgotchi demo`: a throwaway repo where you and some AI agents commit
+while the pet haunts it."""
+import os

+

+
+from gitgotchi.db.state_manager import StateManager
+from gitgotchi.haunt import haunt
+
+CLAUDE = "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"
+COPILOT = "Co-authored-by: Copilot <175728472+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>"
+
+SCRIPT = [
+    ("pumpkin.py", "feat: carve the first pumpkin", None),
+    ("candle.py", "feat: light a candle inside the pumpkin", CLAUDE),
+    ("tests/test_candle.py", "test: make sure the candle stays lit", None),
+    ("lantern.py", "feat: hang a haunted lantern on the porch", CLAUDE),
+    ("walls.py", "fix: ghosts no longer walk through walls", COPILOT),
+    ("bats.py", "feat: summon a friendly bat colony", CLAUDE),
+    ("SPELLBOOK.md", "docs: write down every spell in the spellbook", None),
+    ("crypt.py", "refactor: tidy up the crypt", CLAUDE),
+    ("tests/test_bats.py", "test: count the bats at midnight", CLAUDE),
+    ("cauldron.py", "feat: make the cauldron bubble", COPILOT),
+]
+
+
+def _commit(root: Path, path: str, message: str, trailer) -> None:
+    target = root / path
+    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    target.write_text(f"# {message}\nSPOOKY = True\n")
+    body = f"{message}\n\n{trailer}" if trailer else message
+    subprocess.run(["git", "add", "-A"], cwd=root, check=True, capture_output=True)
+    subprocess.run(["git", "commit", "-q", "-m", body], cwd=root, check=True, capture_output=True)
+
+
+def run_demo(interval: float = 2.8, fps: int = 12) -> None:
+    root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="gitgotchi-demo-"))
+    cwd = os.getcwd()
+    stop = threading.Event()
+    try:
+        repo = Repo.init(root)
+        with repo.config_writer() as cw:
+            cw.set_value("user", "name", "You")
+            cw.set_value("user", "email", "you@example.com")
+            cw.set_value("commit", "gpgsign", "false")
+        os.chdir(root)
+        state = StateManager()
+        stats = state.get_pet_state()
+        stats.pet_name = "Pumpkin"
+        state.save_pet_state(stats)
+
+        def committer():
+            if stop.wait(2.0):
+                return
+            for path, message, trailer in SCRIPT:
+                _commit(root, path, message, trailer)
+                if stop.wait(interval):
+                    return
+
+        threading.Thread(target=committer, daemon=True).start()
+        haunt(Repo(root), state, fps=fps, grace=0.2)
+    finally:
+        stop.set()
+        time.sleep(0.1)
+        os.chdir(cwd)
+        shutil.rmtree(root, ignore_errors=True)

gold:
Fix haunt, seance and history edge cases

- haunt watches every local branch, ignores commits that arrived by
  pull, groups bursts into one reaction, survives a busy database, and
  doesn't treat commit messages as Rich markup
- history uses --no-renames and unquotes non-ASCII paths; the witching
  hour uses the author's own timezone
- the seance blames each file once and skips files it can't blame
- the demo waits for its committer and closes the database before cleanup
- hook output can't be broken by markup in the pet's name

+RESET = "\x1b[0m"

+def find_state_db(start: Path) -> Optional[Path]:
+    """The pet database for the repo containing `start`, if there is one."""
+    for folder in [start, *start.parents]:
+        dot_git = folder / ".git"
+        if dot_git.is_dir():
+            git_dir = dot_git
+        elif dot_git.is_file():
+            # A linked worktree: .git is a file pointing at the real git dir
+            pointer = dot_git.read_text().strip()
+            if not pointer.startswith("gitdir:"):
+                return None
+            git_dir = (folder / pointer[len("gitdir:"):].strip()).resolve()
+        else:
+            continue
+
+        common = git_dir
+        commondir = git_dir / "commondir"
+        if commondir.is_file():
+            common = (git_dir / commondir.read_text().strip()).resolve()
+
+        for candidate in (common / "gitgotchi" / "state.db", folder / ".gitgotchi" / "state.db"):
+            if candidate.is_file():
+                return candidate
+        return None
+    return None
+
+
+def load_stats(db: Path) -> Optional[PetStats]:
+    try:
+        conn = sqlite3.connect(_sqlite_uri(db), uri=True, timeout=1)
+    except sqlite3.Error:
+        return None
+    try:
+        conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
+        row = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM pet_state LIMIT 1").fetchone()
+    except sqlite3.Error:
+        return None
+    finally:
+        conn.close()
+    if row is None:
+        return None
+
+    columns = row.keys()
+    stats = PetStats()
+    stats.pet_name = row["pet_name"]
+    stats.total_commits = row["total_commits"] or 0
+    stats.ai_commits = (row["ai_commits"] if "ai_commits" in columns else 0) or 0
+    stats.quality_score = row["quality_score"] or 50.0
+    stats.current_form = PetForm(row["current_form"])
+    stats.last_fed = _parse_time(row["last_fed"]) or datetime.now()
+    if "last_visit" in columns:
+        stats.last_visit = _parse_time(row["last_visit"])

+    return stats
+

+def render_line(stats: PetStats, color: bool = True) -> str:
+    info = theme.form_info(stats.current_form)

+        if not color:

+

+Claude Code: add this to ~/.claude/settings.json
+  "statusLine": {"type": "command", "command": "gitgotchi-statusline"}
+

+# bostonmove
+
+Getting around Boston from live public data: MBTA departures and service alerts, Bluebikes bike and dock
+counts, and simple door-to-door options (walk, Bluebikes, or one direct MBTA route). A command-line tool
+and an MCP server, so Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor and other agents can answer "when's the next
+train" or "is there a dock near Kendall" with real numbers. It only reads public data.
+
+```
+$ bostonmove plan "South Station" "Kendall"
+South Station  →  Kendall/MIT  (2784 m straight line)
+   12 min  Red Line to Alewife: board at South Station (0 min walk) in 6 min, ride 6, off at Kendall/MIT  (arrive ~13:27)
+   18 min  Bluebikes from Surface Rd at Summer St (26 bikes) to Kendall T (10 docks)  (arrive ~13:33)
+   43 min  walk, about 3620 m  (arrive ~13:58)
+  · Walking and cycling times are estimates from straight-line distance; transit times are from MBTA live predictions, or the timetable when there are none.
+  · Direct routes only: this doesn't plan transfers yet (mbta.com/trip-planner does).
+```
+
+## Install
+
+From a clone, until it's on PyPI:
+
+```bash
+uv tool install .
+```
+
+Add it to Claude Code:
+
+```bash
+claude mcp add bostonmove -- bostonmove mcp
+```
+
+Or in any MCP client's config:
+
+```json
+{ "mcpServers": { "bostonmove": { "command": "bostonmove", "args": ["mcp"] } } }
+```
+
+**MBTA API key (optional, free).** Without one the MBTA allows 20 requests a minute, which a couple of trip
+plans can use up. With a key from [api-v3.mbta.com](https://api-v3.mbta.com) it's 1,000. Set `MBTA_API_KEY`
+in the environment, or pass it in the MCP config with `"env": {"MBTA_API_KEY": "..."}`. When the limit is hit,
+bostonmove says so; `plan_trip` still returns the walking and Bluebikes options.
+
+## Tools
+
+| MCP tool | CLI | What it answers |
+|---|---|---|
+| `next_departures` | `bostonmove next "Park Street" [--route Red]` | Upcoming departures at a stop by route and direction: live when the MBTA has predictions, else the timetable, plus alerts at that stop |
+| `service_alerts` | `bostonmove alerts [--route Orange] [--stop X]` | Delays, suspensions, shuttles, detours and closures in effect now, most severe first |
+| `bike_availability` | `bostonmove bikes "Kendall" [--need bike\|ebike\|dock]` | Nearest Bluebikes stations with bikes, e-bikes and free docks |
+| `find_nearby` | `bostonmove near "Fenway Park"` | MBTA stations and stops, and Bluebikes stations, near a place |
+| `plan_trip` | `bostonmove plan A B` | Walk, Bluebikes and direct MBTA options with arrival times |
+
+A place can be a station name (`Park Street`, `Kendall`, `Northeastern`), an MBTA stop id (`place-pktrm`,

+Every result carries `sources` and `as_of`. Add `--json` to any CLI command for the full result.
+

gold:
Plan one change between subway and light-rail lines

plan_trip now looks for a line near the start and a line near the destination
that share a station, ranks the pairs by walking plus stops travelled, and
prices the best two with live departures, leaving 3 minutes to change. Changes
are only priced when no subway or light-rail line goes the whole way.

Each leg is now one request: predictions (or the next 90 minutes of the
timetable) at both stops, paired up by trip. A plan costs 4 to 16 MBTA requests
instead of up to 30, and on the keyless limit the client waits up to 20 s for
the count to reset rather than fail. Transit options are reported as legs.

@@ -0,0 +1,146 @@
+"""Build the site's data from the raw sources: roll calls, councillors and a summary, as JSON in web/data/.
+
+boston.gov's roll-call pages are the primary source where they have been fetched; the open dataset fills
+in what they don't cover and is compared with them where both have a roll call (matched on date and
+docket number). Every derived number on the site comes from these files.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import glob
+import json
+import os
+import re
+from collections import Counter
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+
+from . import checks, clean, parse
+from .sources import RAW, ROLLCALL_URL, ROOT
+
+OUT = os.path.join(ROOT, "web", "data")
+DATASET_URL = "https://data.boston.gov/dataset/city-council-roll-call-votes"
+KINDS = ["yes", "no", "present", "abstain", "absent"]
+
+
+def load_sources() -> tuple[list[parse.RollCall], list[parse.RollCall]]:
+    gov = []
+    for path in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(RAW, "bostongov", "page-*.html"))):
+        with open(path) as f:
+            gov += parse.parse_rollcall_page(f.read())
+    seen, unique = set(), []
+    for r in gov:  # a page fetched twice, or an entry that shifted pages between fetches
+        if r.source_id not in seen:
+            seen.add(r.source_id)
+            unique.append(r)
+    data_path = os.path.join(RAW, "opendata.json")
+    od = parse.parse_opendata(json.load(open(data_path))) if os.path.exists(data_path) else []
+    return unique, od
+
+
+def title(description: str, docket: str) -> str:
+    """The motion in a line: the description up to its first full stop, without the procedural opening."""
+    t = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", description).strip()
+    t = re.sub(rf"^0*{int(docket) if docket.isdigit() else re.escape(docket)}\s+", "", t)
+    date = r"(?:January|February|March|April|May|June|July|August|September|October|November|December)\s+\d{1,2},?\s+\d{4}"
+    t = re.sub(r"^Councill?ors?\s+[^,]+?\s+called\s+Docket\s*#\s*\d+,\s*", "", t, flags=re.I)
+    t = re.sub(r"^Councill?ors?\s+.{0,300}?\boffered the following:?\s*", "", t, flags=re.I)
+    t = re.sub(rf"^On the (message and (order|ordinance)|petition|communication|order|report)[^,]*?,?\s*"
+               rf"(referred(?: on)?\s+{date},?\s*)?(Docket\s*#\s*\d+,?\s*)?", "", t, flags=re.I)
+    t = re.sub(rf"^(referred(?: on)?\s+{date},?\s*)?Docket\s*#\s*\d+,?\s*", "", t, flags=re.I)
+    t = re.sub(r"^(message and order|message and ordinance|order)\s+for\s+(your|you)\s+approval,?\s*(an?\s+)?",
+               "", t, flags=re.I)
+    # "the amount of Two Hundred Thousand Dollars ($200,000.00)" -> "$200,000.00"; the figure is the record's
+    words = (r"(?:(?:One|Two|Three|Four|Five|Six|Seven|Eight|Nine|Ten|Eleven|Twelve|Thirteen|Fourteen|Fifteen|"
+             r"Sixteen|Seventeen|Eighteen|Nineteen|Twenty|Thirty|Forty|Fifty|Sixty|Seventy|Eighty|Ninety|Hundred|"
+             r"Thousand|Million|Billion|and)[\s-]*)+")
+    spelled = rf"{words}Dollars(?:\s+and\s+{words}Cents)?"
+    t = re.sub(r"\bin the amount of\b", "of", t, flags=re.I)
+    t = re.sub(rf"(?:the amount of\s+)?\(?{spelled}\)?\s*\((\$[\d,.]+)\)", r"\1", t, flags=re.I)
+    t = re.sub(rf"\((\$[\d,.]+)\)\s*\({spelled}\)", r"\1", t, flags=re.I)
+    t = re.sub(r"^Message and (order|ordinance)\s+(?=(to|for|approving|authorizing|declaring|amending)\b)", "",
+               t, flags=re.I)
+    first = re.split(r"(?<=[a-z0-9)\"”])\.\s+(?=[A-Z])", t, maxsplit=1)[0]
+    first = first[0].upper() + first[1:] if first else first
+    return first if len(first) <= 180 else first[:177].rsplit(" ", 1)[0] + "…"
+
+
+def outcome(description: str) -> str:
+    """The clerk's closing sentence, which states what happened and the tally."""
+    t = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", description).strip()
+    parts = re.split(r"(?<=[.;])\s+", t)
+    with_tally = [p for p in parts if re.search(r"\byeas?\b", p, flags=re.I)]
+    return (with_tally[-1] if with_tally else parts[-1]).strip()
+
+
+def build() -> dict:
+    gov, od = load_sources()
+    rolls_raw = gov + [r for r in od if (r.date, r.docket.lstrip("0")) not in
+                       {(g.date, g.docket.lstrip("0")) for g in gov}]
+    cleaned, people = clean.clean(rolls_raw)
+    known = {p.split("-")[0] for p in people}
+    od_by_key = {}
+    if gov:
+        od_clean, _ = clean.clean(od)
+        for r in od_clean:
+            od_by_key.setdefault((r.date, r.docket.lstrip("0")), []).append(r)
+
+    rolls = []
+    for r in sorted(cleaned, key=lambda x: (x.date, x.source_id), reverse=True):
+        counts = Counter(v.vote for v in r.votes)
+        problems = checks.check(r, known)
+        twin = od_by_key.get((r.date, r.docket.lstrip("0")), []) if r.source == "bostongov" else []
+        if len(twin) == 1:
+            a = {(v.councillor, v.vote) for v in r.votes}
+            b = {(v.councillor, v.vote) for v in twin[0].votes}
+            if a != b:
+                problems.append("The open dataset records this roll call differently: " + ", ".join(
+                    f"{c} {v}" for c, v in sorted(b - a)) + ".")
+        rolls.append({

+name: Update votes
+
+# Every morning: fetch the newest roll-call pages from boston.gov, rebuild the site's data, run the tests,
+# and commit if anything changed. The host redeploys the site from that commit. If boston.gov hasn't
+# answered for a week, the run fails, and GitHub emails the repository's owner.
+on:
+  schedule:
+    - cron: "17 11 * * *"   # 07:17 in Boston in summer, 06:17 in winter
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: write
+
+concurrency:
+  group: update
+  cancel-in-progress: false
+
+jobs:
+  update:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 30
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v6
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - run: uv sync --frozen
+      - name: Fetch and build
+        id: update
+        run: uv run councilvotes update
+        continue-on-error: true
+      - run: uv run pytest -q
+      - name: Commit what changed
+        run: |
+          git config user.name "council-votes bot"
+          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
+          git add data/raw web/data web/public/index.json
+          if git diff --cached --quiet; then echo "No change"; exit 0; fi
+          git commit -m "Update votes $(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)"
+          git push
+      - name: Fail if boston.gov has been unreachable for a week
+        if: steps.update.outcome == 'failure'
+        run: exit 1

@@ -0,0 +1,65 @@
+# Yeas & Nays
+
+Every recorded roll-call vote of the Boston City Council since 2008, as a site you can search: how each
+councillor voted, which votes split the Council, who votes with whom, and the records where the City's own
+data contradicts itself.
+
+An independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by the City of Boston.
+
+## Where the votes come from
+
+| Source | What it has | Licence |
+|---|---|---|
+| [boston.gov roll-call votes](https://www.boston.gov/departments/city-council/city-council-roll-call-votes) | Every roll call since 2008 with each councillor's vote, still updated | City of Boston terms of use, which allow republishing City information without implying endorsement |
+| [Analyze Boston: City Council Roll Call Votes](https://data.boston.gov/dataset/city-council-roll-call-votes) | 1,235 roll calls, January 2008 to March 2024, one row per councillor's vote | Open Data Commons PDDL (public domain) |
+
+boston.gov is the main source; the dataset fills in what hasn't been fetched from it and is compared with it
+where both have a roll call. Raw responses are kept in `data/raw/`, so every number on the site can be traced
+to what the City published. Pages are fetched three seconds apart with an identifying user agent, and the
+daily run fetches only the newest three pages. Meeting video is not copied; YouTube's terms don't allow it.
+
+## What is changed, and what is checked
+
+The records name councillors by surname and use short codes for votes. To join them up, `clean.py` reads
+misspelled surnames as the councillor they refer to, drops vacant seats, keeps a council president election's
+votes as choices, and resolves a stray letter in a name field only when exactly one councillor who voted
+elsewhere that day is missing. A surname that vanishes for over a year and returns is listed as two stretches,
+because the data can't tell a returning councillor from a new one with the same name. Every change is written
+on the roll call's own page.
+

+# Hearth
+
+A clean home screen for Amazon Fire TV. No sponsored rows, no autoplaying ads, no tracking: your apps, a clock,
+and a glow in the colour of whatever you're about to watch.
+
+| Before | After |
+|---|---|
+| ![Stock Fire TV home with a sponsored banner](docs/before.jpg) | ![Hearth with the Ember theme](docs/after-ember.jpg) |
+
+Fire OS won't let another app become Home, so Hearth doesn't fight it: a small accessibility service watches for
+Amazon's home screen and opens Hearth in its place. Amazon's launcher stays installed and enabled, and pressing
+Home twice in a row still gets you to it.
+
+## What it does
+
+- **Debloat.** Disables Amazon's content recognition (ACR), shopping, telemetry, tutorials and preloads with
+  `pm disable-user`. Nothing is uninstalled and everything comes back with one command.
+- **Home.** Builds the launcher from source and installs it, with `FireHomeService` sending the Home button to it.
+  The service only sees window changes from Amazon's launcher and Appstore. It reads no screen content and filters
+  no keys, so held Volume keeps repeating.
+- **Ad-blocking DNS**, optional: Private DNS through AdGuard for the whole TV.
+- **Themes** you can switch without a rebuild.
+
+## Install
+
+On the TV: Settings > My Fire TV > About, press OK on the first entry seven times, then back to Developer options
+and switch **ADB debugging** on.
+
+On a Mac or Linux machine on the same network, with JDK 17 and the Android SDK (platform 34, build-tools 34.0.0):
+
+```bash
+TV_HOST=192.168.1.50 DNS=1 THEME=themes/ember ./install.sh
+```
+
+Accept "Allow USB debugging?" on the TV when it asks. The script backs up the TV's packages and settings to
+`backup/`, applies the debloat list for your model if there is one in `lists/`, builds and installs the launcher,

Fire OS 8.1.8.5.

crossfade between two players, so the seam never shows. The Fireplace tile
opens it with sound; "fireplace" in a theme makes it Home's idle screen,
silent. install.sh downloads the clip; it is not stored in the repo. The
screen is held on for 3 hours from the tile and 30 minutes from idle, then
the TV may sleep as usual. Ember turns it on after 3 idle minutes.

+name: Release
+
+# Push a tag like v0.2.0 to build a signed APK and attach it to a GitHub release.
+# Signing uses the repository secrets HEARTH_KEYSTORE_B64 (base64 of the .jks) and HEARTH_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD;
+# without them the APK is signed with a throwaway debug key and will not install over an earlier release.
+on:
+  push:
+    tags: ['v*']
+
+permissions:
+  contents: write
+
+jobs:
+  release:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
+        with:
+          distribution: temurin
+          java-version: 17
+          cache: gradle
+      - name: Signing key
+        env:
+          KEYSTORE_B64: ${{ secrets.HEARTH_KEYSTORE_B64 }}
+          KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.HEARTH_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
+        run: |
+          if [ -n "$KEYSTORE_B64" ]; then
+            echo "$KEYSTORE_B64" | base64 -d > "$RUNNER_TEMP/hearth.jks"
+            printf 'storeFile=%s\nstorePassword=%s\nkeyAlias=hearth\nkeyPassword=%s\n' \
+              "$RUNNER_TEMP/hearth.jks" "$KEYSTORE_PASSWORD" "$KEYSTORE_PASSWORD" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/signing.properties"
+            echo "HEARTH_SIGNING=$RUNNER_TEMP/signing.properties" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
+          else
+            echo "::warning::No signing secrets: this APK is debug-signed."
+          fi
+      - name: Build
+        working-directory: launcher
+        run: |
+          version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
+          IFS=. read -r major minor patch <<< "$version"
+          code=$(( major * 10000 + minor * 100 + ${patch:-0} ))
+          echo "sdk.dir=$ANDROID_HOME" > local.properties
+          ./gradlew --no-daemon -PhearthVersionName="$version" -PhearthVersionCode="$code" testReleaseUnitTest assembleRelease
+          cp app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk "$RUNNER_TEMP/hearth-$version.apk"
+      - name: Publish
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+        run: gh release create "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" "$RUNNER_TEMP/hearth-${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}.apk" --title "Hearth $GITHUB_REF_NAME" --generate-notes

+# gitwhy
+
+**What just happened to my Git repository, and how do I fix it?**
+
+gitwhy looks at a Git repository and tells you, in plain English, what state it is in and
+which commands will get you out of it: a merge conflict, a rebase stopped halfway, a detached
+HEAD, a rejected push, a login GitHub won't accept, a 120 MB CSV that GitHub will refuse.
+Paste it an error message and it explains that too.
+
+It is written for people meeting Git for the first time. Git's own messages are accurate
+but hard to read; gitwhy turns them into a short explanation and the exact fix.
+
+It only ever **reads** your repository. It never runs the fixes it suggests, so you stay in
+control and learn the commands as you go.
+
+There are two ways to use it, built on the same engine:
+
+- **On the command line**, with no AI tools involved: `gitwhy`.
+- **As an MCP server**, so an assistant such as Claude Code, Claude Desktop or Cursor gets a
+  reliable diagnosis instead of guessing from `git status`.
+
+## Install
+
+gitwhy needs Python 3.10 or newer and Git. Pick one:
+
+```
+uv tool install gitwhy     # with uv (https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)
+pipx install gitwhy        # with pipx
+uvx gitwhy                 # run once without installing
+```
+
+This works the same on macOS, Windows and Linux.
+
+## Use it from the terminal
+
+Run it inside your project folder:
+
+```
+gitwhy                    # what's wrong here, most urgent first
+gitwhy status             # a plain summary: branch, upstream, what's changed
+gitwhy explain "fatal: refusing to merge unrelated histories"
+git push 2>&1 | gitwhy explain -
+```
+
+Options: `--path <folder>` (or `-C`) to look at another folder, `--json` for machine-readable
+output, `--no-color` to turn off colour. Colour is only used in a real terminal and never
+when `NO_COLOR` is set.
+
+Exit codes: `0` nothing blocking, `1` something blocking was found, `2` bad usage (for example
+the folder does not exist), `3` `explain` did not recognise the message.
+
+### Example
+
+```
+$ gitwhy
+gitwhy: /Users/sam/ds3500/hw2 (branch main)
+
+[BLOCKING] Merge in progress with conflicts in 1 file
+  Git tried to combine two lines of work, but both changed the same part of these
+  files, so it stopped and is waiting for you to choose what the result should be.
+  Nothing is lost while you decide.
+  Conflicted files:
+    - analysis.py  (both changed)
+  How to fix:
+    Finish the merge:
+      1. Open each file and find the blocks between <<<<<<< and >>>>>>>. The part
+         above ======= is one version, the part below is the other. Keep what you
+         want, and delete the three marker lines.
+      2. git add analysis.py
+         Marks the files as resolved
+      3. git commit --no-edit
+         Records the merge and finishes it
+    Or cancel the merge:
+      1. git merge --abort
+         Puts everything back the way it was before the merge started
+  Learn more: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-merge#_how_to_resolve_conflicts
+
+1 blocking. gitwhy never runs these commands for you; copy the ones you want.
+```
+
+Commands that can lose work (`git restore`, `git rebase --skip`, `git push --force-with-lease`
+and so on) are always marked with a warning, and a safer option is listed first when one
+exists.
+
+## Use it with an AI assistant (MCP)
+
+`gitwhy mcp` runs a Model Context Protocol server over stdio with three read-only tools:
+
+| Tool | Use it when | Returns |
+|---|---|---|
+| `diagnose_repo(path=".")` | something seems stuck or broken | every problem found, most urgent first, with explanation and fix |
+| `explain_git_error(error_text, path=None)` | a git command printed an error | what the error means and the fix, using the repository's state if `path` is given |
+| `explain_state(path=".")` | you want a neutral summary | branch, upstream, ahead/behind, remotes, staged and changed files, operations in progress |
+
+Results are small JSON objects. Pass an absolute path: relative paths resolve against the
+server's working directory, which for desktop apps is usually not your project. `~` works.
+
+### Claude Code
+
+```
+claude mcp add --scope user gitwhy -- uvx gitwhy mcp
+```
+
+`--scope user` makes it available in every project; leave it out to add it to the current
+project only. Check it with `claude mcp list`.
+

+# Releasing
+
+Publishing is tag-based: pushing a `v*` tag builds the package and uploads it to PyPI through
+trusted publishing (no API token is stored anywhere).
+
+One-time setup on PyPI: Account → Publishing → add a pending publisher with
+project `gitwhy`, owner `Srikarmk`, repository `gitwhy`, workflow `publish.yml`, environment `pypi`.
+
+Each release:
+
+1. Bump the version in both `pyproject.toml` and `src/gitwhy/__init__.py` (the workflow refuses a mismatch).
